title: Truly was not at all what I expected it to be- but also so good?  So ...
transcript: One of my dark theater confessions is that before this production, I had actually never seen or read A Streetcar Named Desire. I didn't even really know what it was about outside the fact that it was a classic and that a guy screams Stella at some point. Like, for some reason, I always thought that this was, like, a steamy romance play. Something about the title Streetcar Named Desire just kind of gives that, like, vibe to me. But it is very much not. It is a dark tragedy drama that deals with some really heavy themes like D V S A, mental health. So much darker than I was expecting it to be. But all of that being said, oftentimes I will see classics, and I'll come out of it saying, really? Like, that was it. That's what all of the fuss was about. A lot of them just feel like products of their time. And honestly, I was very surprised that I did not feel that way about streetcar. In fact, by all accounts, this feels like a very modern play that could have been written yesterday. And of course, part of that is due to Rebecca Freckle staging, which is very modern in its approach. The set is incredibly minimalist and exists in this kind of abstract space, the kind of staging that has become very popular, particularly in Europe, in the past decade or so. But also the inclusion of those darker themes that I Mentioned earlier, not only were those topics just not talked about as much in 1947 as they are today, but also our understanding of them has progressed so much since the 40s. So while, yes, it is helped out by a very modern staging, I do think the play itself holds up to modern audiences more so than a lot of other classics in the canon. And of course, I also have to mention the two lead performances from Paul Mescal and Patsy Ferran. Paul, of course, an incredibly accomplished actor. He's Oscar nominated, so I was familiar with him, but I was not familiar with Patsy Ferran before this. Let me tell you, I will now go see anything she does because she is giving a phenomenal performance in this play. Of course, Paul is excellent as well. I really do think this is a fantastic production of a fantastic play, and you should jump at the opportunity to see this if you can.
